title: Slice the Pizza
bigIdea: A share is a small slice of ownership in a company.

steps.prompt: You own 1 of 100 slices of a pizza shop. What do you actually own?
steps.reveal: A share is a slice of the whole company, not a product. One slice out of 100 is 1% of the shop.

cards.title: A share is a slice
cards.body: A share (also called a stock) is a small piece of ownership in a company. Own one share and you own a tiny part of the whole business.

cards.title: Why companies sell shares
cards.body: Selling shares is one way a company raises cash to grow, without borrowing. Buyers get ownership; the company gets money.

cards.title: What the founder gives up
cards.body: Every share sold is a slice handed to someone else. The founder ends up owning a smaller percentage of a (hopefully) bigger company.

steps.goal: Raise $400 for a better cart, but keep at least 51% of your lemonade stand. (Simulation.)

steps.prompt: Why did your ownership percentage drop after you sold shares?

options.text: You traded away part of the company in exchange for cash
The price of lemonade went down
You still own 100%, the number just looks smaller

steps.explanation: Selling shares trades ownership for cash. Giving up slices means you own a smaller percentage. That trade-off is called dilution.
